title: Simultaneous Brightfield, Fluorescence, and Optical Coherence Tomographic Imaging of Contracting Cardiac Trabeculae Ex Vivo
protocol: Fill the measurement chamber with distilled water.
Place a diffraction grating with known lines per µm into the measurement chamber.
Press F1 to enable capture and adjust Frame Rate [Hz] until the diffraction grating is clearly visible.
Ensure that the diffraction grating runs parallel with the edge of the frame.
Press F1 again to stop capture.
Set Total Images to Capture? to one, press Ctrl + Shift + S to stream data to disk, and press F1 to capture an image of the diffraction grating.
Open ImageJ and import the diffraction grating image (File > Open).
Holding shift, draw a line that encompasses 20 light and dark bands of the diffraction grating.
Calibrate the image (Analyze > Set Scale).
Measure the thickness of a glass microscope slide using Vernier calipers.
Turn on the OCT laser source.
Cover the galvanometer head and click Get BG to measure the background interference pattern.
Clamp the measured glass microscope slide in the measurement arm of the OCT.
Click Live Stream to view the OCT image.
Adjust the glass microscope slide until it is visible within the B-scan.
Set Range Y (Steps) to one.
Click Stream B-scan Data?.
Click Acquire.
Import the B-scan image into ImageJ (File > Open > Select B-scan).
Hold shift and draw a line between the boundaries of the glass microscope slide.
Set the scale (Analyze > Set Scale).
Set Known Distance to the measurement collected in Step 1.2.1.
Correct for the refractive index of the microscope slide by multiplying the measurement per pixel value by nglass.
Pour dissection solution into a small metal bowl and place it in the freezer about an hour before heart excision.
Setup a dissection rig ensuring dissection solution is well-oxygenated with 100% oxygen.
Flush through each tubing line of the dissection rig.
Fill the dissection chamber with oxygenated dissection solution.
Loosely tie 3/0 suture around the perfusion catheter.
Anesthetize 8-10 weeks old Wistar rat using gaseous isoflurane (< 5% in oxygen).
Confirm anesthesia by tail pinching.
Position the anesthetized rat in a supine position.
Inject subcutaneously in the abdominal area with heparin solution (1000 IU/kg).
Maintain anesthesia for five more minutes to allow the heparin to circulate.
Retrieve the metal bowl containing dissection solution from the freezer and place it near the euthanization bench.
Transfer the anesthetized rat to the euthanization bench.
Euthanize by cervical dislocation.
Open the rat chest with scissors, first cutting the body wall along the underside of the ribcage.
Cut the diaphragm next.
Proceed along the lateral borders of the ribcage.
Lift the chest out of the way.
Grab the heart with one hand while using a pair of curved scissors to cut the connecting vessels (aorta, vena cava, etc.) with the other hand.
Quickly submerge the heart in the cold dissection solution.
Identify the aorta while the heart is in the metal bowl.
Transfer the heart to the dissection chamber.
Use two curved forceps to pull the aorta over the perfusion cannula.
Hold the aorta in place with one forceps.
Open the tubing line to allow the dissection solution to flow through the perfusion cannula.
Clear the coronary vasculature of blood and perfuse the heart with dissection solution until completely cleared of blood.
Secure the aorta in place using a suture after stopping the perfusion flow.
Perfuse the cannulated heart and rotate the cannula so that the left coronary artery is visible on the superior surface.
Pin the apex of the heart to the bottom of the dissection chamber.
Cut off both atria from the heart.
With spring scissors, cut along the right side of the septum to the apex of the heart.
Pin the opened left ventricle to the base of the dissection chamber.
Cut along the left side of the septum and open the right ventricle.
Pin the opened right ventricle to the base of the dissection chamber.
Identify a free-running trabecula in the right ventricle.
Using spring scissors and forceps, cut the wall tissue surrounding the trabecula orthogonally to its direction.
Trim the wall tissue until its dimension is appropriate for the mounting configuration.
Prepare the cardiomyometer.
Flush hot (~60 °C) water through the measurement chamber.
Flush distilled water (room temperature) through the measurement chamber.
Flush superfusate solution through the measurement chamber.
Continuously bubble the superfusate solution with carbogen.
Turn on the brightfield microscope illumination source.
Press F1 to enable capture.
Manually adjust the downstream hook until it is centered in the brightfield image.
Click Zero Downstream Axis.
Click Downstream Disabled to enable the motor.
Move the DS Setpoint [um] slider until the end of the hook aligns with the edge of the default region of interest.
Re-zero the downstream axis.
Move the DS Setpoint [um] slider to 1000.
Repeat the process with the upstream hook, but do not move the US Setpoint [um] slider.
Click Move to Mounting.
Start the fluorescence illumination system by toggling the Lamp switch.
Quickly turn on the controller subsystems by toggling the Main switch.
Mount the trabecula.
Pause superfusate flow through the measurement chamber.
Fill the mounting chamber with the dissection solution.
Transport the trabecula from the dissection chamber to the mounting chamber using a 1 mL syringe.
Place the syringe vertically and in contact with the surface of the mounting chamber solution.
Allow the trabecula to descend into the mounting chamber via gravity.
Lower the fluid level in the mounting chamber so that it is level with the midsection of the hooks.
Adjust the distance between the hooks to reflect the slack length of the trabecula by moving the DS Setpoint [um] slider.
Lightly grip one piece of end tissue with forceps and mount it onto the upstream hook.
Mount the other piece of end tissue onto the downstream hook.
Move the trabecula back into the measurement chamber by pressing Move to Chamber.
Resume superfusate flow and fluid extraction.
Set Stimulus frequency [Hz] to 1, Stimulus duration [ms] to 10, and Stimulus Voltage to 10.
Start stimulation by pressing Stimulus On?.
Gradually decrease the stimulus voltage and stimulus duration in 1 V and 1 ms steps after about 1 hour of acclimatization.
Turn on the brightfield illumination system.
Press F1 and select a region of interest that encloses a striated area on the user interface.
Click Compute SL? to calculate the average sarcomere length in the highlighted region.
Increase the muscle length until the average sarcomere length is 2.32 µm by increasing the Separation Setpoint [um] slider.
Move the muscle by adjusting the Centre Setpoint [um] slider on the "Centre and Separation Control tab so that the edge of the downstream hook is just visible within the brightfield image.
Collect the fluorescence information for ten twitches.
Increase the Centre Setpoint [um] value by 200 and collect another ten twitches worth of fluorescence information.
Repeat this process until the brightfield image contains the upstream hook.
Collect the final window's worth of fluorescence information.
Return the trabecula to a central position by setting the Centre Setpoint [um] value to 0.
Reduce the stimulus frequency to 0.2 Hz.
Switch from the KH superfusate to the Fura-2 loading solution.
Measure the fluorescence signal every 10 min by clicking Enable Fluorescence Source on the Stim and Data tab.
Visualize the fluorescence signal on the PMT Signal tab.
Return the stimulus frequency to 1 Hz and switch back to the KH superfusate solution when the 360 nm signal has increased by a factor of 10 or after 2 hours.
Check the ratio measurement every 10 min until it stabilizes, then begin data collection.
Collect brightfield- and fluorescence-imaging data.
Return the muscle to its original position where the edge of the downstream hook is just visible in the brightfield image.
Start streaming hardware data by clicking Stream Data to Disk on the Stim and Data tab.
Capture fluorescence information by clicking Enable Fluorescence Source.
Set the capture mode to an external trigger, increase the frame rate to 100 Hz, and set the number of images to capture to 100 on the brightfield imaging user interface.
Record the brightfield imaging data for this window by pressing Ctrl + Shift + S followed by F1.
Increase Centre Setpoint [um] value by 200 and repeat the previous steps.
Return the trabecula to a central position by setting the Centre Setpoint [um] value to 0.
Collect OCT imaging data.
Turn on the OCT laser source by turning the master key to the | symbol.
Press the power button, followed by the SLDs button.
Cover the galvanometer head and click Get BG to measure the background interference pattern and subtract it from the measurement.
Set the image capture mode to live-view.
Adjust the y-position until the B-scan image contains the upstream hook only.
Divide the muscle length displayed on the control front panel by two and subtract the current y-position.
Enter this value into the "y-offset" input.
Adjust the "x-offset" value until the cross-section of the trabecula is centered in the frame.
With the trabecula centered, scan along the y-axis by adjusting the y-position to find the positions corresponding to the upstream and downstream hooks.
Note these positions down.
Set Range Y (steps) to the absolute difference between these values divided by ten.
Set the image capture mode to Stimulus Triggered?.
Set Range X (steps) to 100.
Click the Set Active Parameters button.
Click Stream B-Scan Data?.
Acquire.
Increase image contrast using Image > Adjust > Brightness/Contrast and centralize the histogram.
Sharpen the images by setting Process > Filters > Unsharp Mask with Radius (Sigma) to 1.0 pixels and Mask Weight (0.1-0.9) to 0.6.
Export the image sequence as PNG format, starting at 0 and using 4 digits for each file name.
Set FolderPath in "TrabeculaProcessing.m" to the main folder containing all data.
Set ImagePath in "TrabeculaProcessing.m" to the folder where the image sequence was saved.
Set sections in "TrabeculaProcessing.m" to the number of imaging windows.
Set frames in "TrabeculaProcessing.m" to the number of frames captured per window.
Run the code in "TrabeculaProcessing.m".
Use image-processing software to perform a FFT on a region with highly visible sarcomeres.
Multiply pixels per µm calibration results by 1.6 µm and 3.0 µm before calculating the inverse for spatial frequencies.
Fit an exponential curve to the FFT result, ignoring certain frequency information.
Subtract the fitted exponential from the transform result to remove the DC term.
Fit a Gaussian curve to the frequency band of interest.
Calculate the inverse of the peak of the Gaussian curve.
Subtract the window-dependent autofluorescence from the respective window.
Compute the quotient of the signals associated with the 340 nm and 380 nm excitation wavelengths.
Open ImageJ and import the OCT images.
Locate the images in the file explorer window.
Select one image and click Open.
Convert the images to PNG if necessary.
Organize the image sequence into a hyperstack.
Set the number of slices to the number of B-scans per slice.
Set the X dimension to the number of slices along the length of the trabecula.
Draw a rectangle that encloses the trabecula.
Confirm that it encloses the entire volume through time using the sliders on the hyperstack window.
Crop the image to the selected window.
Remove slices containing images of the mounting hooks.
Select the range of slices that contains trabecula information only.
Train WEKA segmentation.
Launch WEKA segmentation.
Set selection mode to Freehand.
Adjust classifier and training settings in Settings menu.
Manually segment images until satisfactory results are achieved.
Save the classifier.
Load the classifier from previous step.
Click Create Result.
Convert images to 8-bit (Image > Type > 8-bit).
Convert images to binary (Process > Binary > Make Binary > Default method and default background).
Save as image sequence (PNG).
Count the number of white pixels in a binary B-scan image.
Multiply pixel area by calibrated depth resolution from Step 1.2 and 10 µm.
Repeat for all B-scans between hooks.
Average measurements to calculate average CSA.
Convert segmented image into a mesh.
Open "OCTmain.m".
Set imageDirectory to the folder containing the output from Step 6.3.6.
Set outputPath as necessary.
Set slices to the value of "Range Y (steps)" from Step 3.5.5.
Set frames to the value of "Repeat X" from Step 3.5.6.
Set z_dim to the depth resolution from Step 1.2.10.
Set x_dim and y_dim to the values assigned in Step 10.
Click Run.
